p.i: An account of Lehi, his wife Sariah, and his four sons, named beginning with the oldest Laman, Lemuel, Sam, and Nephi. The Lord warns Lehi to leave the land of Jerusalem because he prophesies to the people about their iniquity and they attempt to kill him. He journeys for three days into the wilderness with his family. Nephi takes his brothers and returns to Jerusalem to get the record of the Jews. The account of their hardships. They marry Ishmael’s daughters. They take their families and depart into the wilderness. Their suffering and troubles in the wilderness. The path of their travels. They come to the ocean. Nephi’s brothers rebel against him. He proves them wrong and builds a ship. They name the place Bountiful. They cross the ocean to the promised land, etc. This is according to Nephi’s account — that is, I Nephi engraved this record.

chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 I Nephi was born to excellent parents. As a consequence, my father taught me from all his knowledge. I’ve experienced many hardships during my life, while at the same time I’ve been greatly blessed by the Lord. I gained great understanding of God’s goodness and mysteries. Therefore I’m making a record of the important events in my life. VerseEnd Verse2 I’m writing in my father’s language, which consists of Jewish knowledge written using Egyptian script. VerseEnd Verse3 I know the record I’m making is true, written in my own hand, and based on what I know and experienced. VerseEnd

Verse4 My father Lehi lived his whole life at Jerusalem. During the first year that Zedekiah king of Judah ruled, many prophets were warning that the people must repent or the great city of Jerusalem would be destroyed. VerseEnd

Verse5 So my father, when he was alone, prayed to the Lord with his whole heart for his people. VerseEnd Verse6 As he prayed to the Lord, a pillar of fire descended and rested on a rock in front of him, and he saw and heard many things. What he saw and heard made him shake and tremble. VerseEnd Verse7 Afterward, he returned to his house in Jerusalem and collapsed on his bed, overwhelmed by the Spirit and what he had seen. VerseEnd Verse8 While overwhelmed by the Spirit, he was carried away in a vision. He saw the heavens open, and he thought he saw God sitting on His throne, surrounded by numberless rings of angels engaged in singing and praising Him. VerseEnd Verse9 He also saw a person descending from heaven who was brighter than the midday sun. VerseEnd Verse10 He then saw twelve others following Him, and they were brighter than the stars in the sky. VerseEnd Verse11 They came down to the earth. The first one came and stood in front of my father and gave him a book and told him to read. VerseEnd Verse12 As he read, he was filled with the Spirit of the Lord. VerseEnd Verse13 He read: Woe, woe to Jerusalem, because I’ve seen 2PSI your abominations! My father continued to read about Jerusalem; that it would be destroyed along with its inhabitants, many would be killed by the sword and many would be captured and taken to Babylon. VerseEnd Verse14 After my father read and saw many great and surprising things, he cried out to the Lord: O Lord God Almighty, 2PSI You’ve done such great and awe-inspiring things! 2PSI Your throne is high in the heavens, and 2PSI Your power, goodness, and mercy are over everyone living on earth. And because 2PSI You are merciful, 2PSI You won’t let those who come to 2PSI You be lost. VerseEnd Verse15 This is an example of how my father praised God. He rejoiced and his heart was full because of what the Lord showed him. VerseEnd

Verse16 Now I won’t provide a full account of what my father wrote since he’s written many things he saw in visions and dreams. He also wrote many prophecies that he told to his children. I’m not including a full account of those things. VerseEnd Verse17 Instead, I’ll write an account of important events in my life. First, I’ll summarize my father’s record on these plates I made with my own hands. Then, following my father’s summarized record, I’ll write an account of my life. VerseEnd

Verse18 After the Lord showed my father Lehi the approaching destruction of Jerusalem and other astonishing things, he started prophesying about what he had seen and heard. VerseEnd Verse19 However, telling them the truth about their wickedness and abominations resulted in the Jews mocking him. But when he also testified that he saw, heard, and read in a book that a Messiah was coming to redeem the world, VerseEnd Verse20 that made the Jews furious with him, just like they were with former prophets, whom they had thrown out, stoned, and killed. So they tried to kill my father too. But the Lord’s tender mercies are shown to everyone He has chosen because of their faith. He uses His power to save their lives. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 Following this, the Lord spoke to my father in a dream and told him: 2PSI You are blessed, Lehi, because of the things 2PSI you’ve done. And because 2PSI you’ve been faithful and declared the things I commanded 2PSI you, they’re trying to kill 2PSI you. VerseEnd Verse2 In that dream, the Lord commanded my father to take his family and make his way into the wilderness. VerseEnd Verse3 He obeyed the Lord’s word and did what the Lord commanded him. VerseEnd

Verse4 He departed into the wilderness. He left his house, the land he had inherited, and his gold, silver, and valuables, and didn’t take anything with him except his family, provisions, and tents, and left into the wilderness. VerseEnd Verse5 He came down by the mountains near the Red Sea shore, journeying through the wilderness until reaching the Borders of the Red Sea. He traveled with his family, consisting of my mother Sariah, and older brothers, who were Laman, Lemuel, and Sam. VerseEnd Verse6 After he traveled for three days across the wilderness, he pitched his tent in a valley by a river. VerseEnd

Verse7 Then he built a stone altar and made an offering to the Lord and gave thanks to the Lord our God. VerseEnd Verse8 My father named the river Laman, and it flowed into the Red Sea. The valley was in the mountainous area near its mouth. VerseEnd Verse9 When my father saw the river emptied into the source of the Red Sea, he said to Laman: I wish 2PSI you would be like this river — always flowing into the source of all righteousness. VerseEnd Verse10 He also said to Lemuel: I wish 2PSI you would be like this valley — firm, resolute, and immovable in keeping the Lord’s commandments. VerseEnd Verse11 He said this because Laman and Lemuel were stubborn. They complained about their father over many things: that he was a man carried away by his imagination, and had taken them away from Jerusalem, making them leave their land, gold, silver, and valuables, only to die in the wilderness. They said he did this because of his foolish, delusional thinking. VerseEnd Verse12 This is how Laman and Lemuel, the oldest children, complained about their father. They complained because they didn’t understand how the God who created them deals with mankind. VerseEnd Verse13 They also didn’t believe the great city of Jerusalem could be destroyed like the prophets were saying. They were like the Jerusalem Jews who tried to kill my father. VerseEnd Verse14 But my father was inspired by the Spirit, speaking to them with such power in the valley of Lemuel that they shook with fear before him. He silenced them and they didn’t dare speak against him. Therefore they submitted to him. VerseEnd Verse15 And my father occupied a tent. VerseEnd

Verse16 Since I was very young — but large in build — and had a strong desire to know about God’s mysteries, I cried to the Lord in prayer. He influenced me and softened my heart letting me believe everything my father had said. As a result, I didn’t rebel against him like my brothers. VerseEnd Verse17 And I talked to Sam, telling him what the Lord had revealed to me by His Holy Spirit. And he believed my words. VerseEnd Verse18 But Laman and Lemuel refused to listen to me. Because their hard-heartedness troubled me, I cried to the Lord in prayer for them. VerseEnd Verse19 And the Lord replied: 2PSI You are blessed, Nephi, because of 2PSI your faith, having honestly approached Me with a humble heart. VerseEnd Verse20 And to the degree 2PP you keep My commandments, 2PP you will prosper and be led to a promised land, one that I’ve prepared for 2PP you, a specially chosen land, better than all other places on earth. VerseEnd Verse21 And to the extent 2PSI your brothers rebel against 2PSI you, they’ll be cut off from the presence of the Lord. VerseEnd Verse22 And to the degree 2PSI you keep My commandments, 2PSI you will be made a ruler and teacher over them. VerseEnd Verse23 When they rebel against Me, I’ll curse them with a severe curse, and they won’t have any power over 2PSI your descendants unless they also rebel against Me. VerseEnd Verse24 And if 2PSI your descendants rebel against Me, 2PSI your brothers’ descendants will afflict 2PSI your descendants to help them remember. VerseEnd

LEChapter3 Verse1 Then I returned from speaking with the Lord to my father’s tent. VerseEnd Verse2 And he said to me: I’ve had a dream where the Lord commanded 2PSI you and 2PSI your brothers to return to Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse3 The assignment is to go to Laban who has the record of the Jews and my forefathers’ genealogy engraved on brass plates. VerseEnd Verse4 The Lord has commanded for 2PSI you and 2PSI your brothers to go to Laban’s house, retrieve the records, and bring them down here in the wilderness. VerseEnd Verse5 2PSI Your brothers are complaining, saying it’s a difficult thing I’ve asked them to do. But I haven’t asked them to do it. To the contrary, it’s a commandment from the Lord. VerseEnd Verse6 So go, my son, and 2PSI you’ll be blessed by the Lord because 2PSI you haven’t complained. VerseEnd Verse7 Then I told my father: I’ll go and do what the Lord has commanded because I know the Lord doesn’t give people any commandments without preparing a way for them to accomplish what He commands to be done. VerseEnd Verse8 When my father heard this, he was very pleased since he could tell my understanding came from the Lord. VerseEnd

Verse9 So my brothers and I returned with our tents back to Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse10 And when we arrived, we discussed among ourselves VerseEnd Verse11 and drew lots for who was to go to Laban’s house. The lot fell on Laman. So he went to Laban’s house and talked with him inside. VerseEnd Verse12 He asked Laban for the records engraved on the brass plates, which contained my father’s genealogy. VerseEnd Verse13 But Laban got angry and threw him out, refusing to give him the records. He accused him: 2PSI You’re a robber! I’m going to kill 2PSI you! VerseEnd Verse14 But Laman ran away and told us what Laban had done. As a result, we were very discouraged, and my brothers were about to return to my father in the wilderness. VerseEnd

Verse15 But I told them: As surely as the Lord lives and we live, we won’t return to our father in the wilderness until we’ve accomplished what the Lord has commanded us to do. VerseEnd Verse16 Therefore let’s be faithful in keeping the Lord’s commandments. Let’s go down to our father’s land, because he left gold, silver, and valuables there. And he left everything because of the Lord’s commandments. VerseEnd Verse17 For he knows Jerusalem will be destroyed because of the people’s wickedness, VerseEnd Verse18 because they’ve rejected the words of the prophets. Therefore if our father were to live in the land after having been commanded to flee, he would lose his life too; that being so, he had to flee from the place. VerseEnd Verse19 And it’s God’s wise plan for us to get these records so we can continue to keep our forefathers’ language for our children VerseEnd Verse20 and preserve the words spoken by all the holy prophets, which have been given to them by the Spirit and power of God, containing everything from when the world began to the present time. VerseEnd Verse21 With these words I persuaded my brothers to be faithful in keeping God’s commandments. VerseEnd

Verse22 So we went down to our land and gathered our gold, silver, and valuables. VerseEnd Verse23 After gathering them, we went back up to Laban’s house. VerseEnd Verse24 We came to see Laban and asked him to give us the records written on the brass plates in exchange for our gold, silver, and valuables. VerseEnd Verse25 When he saw our considerable possessions, he wanted to have them so much that he drove us out by force and sent his servants to kill us so he could steal our property. VerseEnd Verse26 We fled from Laban’s servants and were compelled to drop our possessions, and Laban took them. VerseEnd

Verse27 We escaped into the wilderness where we hid in a cave, and Laban’s servants didn’t catch us. VerseEnd Verse28 Laman was angry with me, and with my father as well — and so was Lemuel, since he listened to Laman. As a result, Laman and Lemuel blamed us, their younger brothers, and they beat us with a club. VerseEnd Verse29 As they were hitting us, an angel of the Lord appeared before them and asked: Why are 2PP you hitting 2PP your younger brother with a club? Don’t 2PP you realize that because of 2PP your iniquities the Lord has chosen him to be 2PP your leader? 2PP You must return to Jerusalem, and the Lord will hand Laban over to 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse30 After the angel said this to us, he left. VerseEnd Verse31 After the angel left, Laman and Lemuel again began to complain: How is it possible the Lord will hand Laban over to us? He’s a powerful man and can command fifty. In fact, he can kill fifty, so why not us? VerseEnd

LEChapter4 Verse1 I said to my brothers: Let’s go back up to Jerusalem and be faithful in keeping the Lord’s commandments. He’s more powerful than the whole earth, so why not more powerful than Laban and his fifty? Or even than his tens of thousands? VerseEnd Verse2 So, let’s go back there. Let’s be strong like Moses, because he actually spoke to the waters of the Red Sea and they divided to the right and left, and our fathers came through on dry ground out of slavery, and Pharaoh’s armies followed and were drowned in the Red Sea. VerseEnd Verse3 Now 2PP you know this is true. And 2PP you also know an angel has spoken to 2PP you. So why do 2PP you doubt? Let’s go back. The Lord can protect us, just like our ancestors, and destroy Laban, just like the Egyptians. VerseEnd

Verse4 When I said this, they were still very angry and kept complaining. Nevertheless, they followed me until we reached the wall of Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse5 It was dark and I had them hide outside the wall. After they concealed themselves, I crept into the city and went toward Laban’s house. VerseEnd Verse6 I was led by the Spirit, not knowing in advance what I would do. VerseEnd Verse7 Nevertheless, I continued on. As I approached Laban’s house, I saw a man on the ground ahead of me who was drunk with wine. VerseEnd Verse8 When I approached him, I saw it was Laban. VerseEnd Verse9 I noticed his sword and removed it from its sheath. Its hilt was made of pure gold and the design was of superior quality. The blade was made from the most expensive steel. VerseEnd

Verse10 And the Spirit urged me to kill Laban. But I said in my heart: I’ve never killed anyone. So I hesitated and drew back, not wanting to kill him. VerseEnd Verse11 But the Spirit told me again: The Lord has handed him over to 2PSI you. And I was also aware he had tried to kill me, and that he refused to listen to and follow the Lord’s commandments, and he had also taken our property. VerseEnd Verse12 Then the Spirit told me again: Kill him — the Lord has handed him over to 2PSI you. VerseEnd Verse13 The Lord kills the wicked to accomplish His righteous purposes. It’s better for one man to lose his life than for a nation to lose their way and fall into unbelief. VerseEnd Verse14 When I had heard these words, I remembered the words the Lord had spoken to me in the wilderness: To the degree 2PSI your descendants keep My commandments, they’ll prosper in the promised land. VerseEnd Verse15 And I also considered that they couldn’t keep the Lord’s commandments of the Law of Moses unless they had the Law. VerseEnd Verse16 And I knew that the Law was engraved on the brass plates. VerseEnd Verse17 Furthermore, I knew the Lord had handed Laban over to me so I could get the records as He commanded. VerseEnd Verse18 So I obeyed the Spirit’s voice, took Laban by the hair of his head, and struck his head with his own sword. VerseEnd

Verse19 After I had cracked his head with his sword, I took Laban’s clothes and put them on. I also secured his armor around my waist. VerseEnd Verse20 After doing this, I went to Laban’s treasury. As I was going there, I saw Laban’s servant who had the treasury keys, and imitating Laban’s voice I ordered him to go with me into the treasury. VerseEnd Verse21 He believed me to be his master Laban since he saw the clothes and the sword fastened around my waist. VerseEnd Verse22 He talked to me about the Jewish elders, knowing his master had been out with them at night. VerseEnd Verse23 And I spoke to him as if I were Laban VerseEnd Verse24 and told him I was going to carry the engravings on the brass plates to my older brothers who were outside the walls. VerseEnd Verse25 I also ordered him to follow me. VerseEnd Verse26 He thought I referred to church elders and I really was Laban whom I had killed, so he followed me. VerseEnd Verse27 He talked to me many times about the Jewish elders as I went to my brothers outside the city wall. VerseEnd

Verse28 When Laman saw me, he was very scared, and so were Lemuel and Sam. They ran away because they thought I was Laban and he had killed me and was coming to kill them too. VerseEnd Verse29 I called after them and they heard me; so they stopped running away. VerseEnd Verse30 When Laban’s servant saw my brothers, he began to shake with fear and was about to run and return to Jerusalem. VerseEnd Verse31 Because I have a large build and had received great strength from the Lord, I grabbed Laban’s servant and held him so he couldn’t run away. VerseEnd

Verse32 I told him that if he would agree with my words, as surely as the Lord lives and I live, if he would agree with what we said, we would spare his life. VerseEnd Verse33 And I took an oath that he didn’t need to be afraid; he would be a free person like we were if he was willing to go down with us into the wilderness. VerseEnd Verse34 I also told him: The Lord has certainly commanded us to do this. So shouldn’t we be diligent in keeping the Lord’s commandment? Therefore if 2PSI you’re willing to go down into the wilderness to my father, 2PSI you’ll have a place with us. VerseEnd Verse35 Then Zoram — which was the servant’s name — was satisfied with what I said and promised to go down into the wilderness to our father. He also made an oath he would stay with us from then on. VerseEnd Verse36 Now we wanted him to stay with us so the Jews wouldn’t know about our sudden departure into the wilderness to follow and kill us. VerseEnd Verse37 But once Zoram took an oath, our worries about him ended. VerseEnd Verse38 So we took the brass plates and Laban’s servant and went into the wilderness, traveling to our father’s tent. VerseEnd

LEChapter5 Verse1 After we came to our father in the wilderness, he was overjoyed. And my mother Sariah was extremely glad because she had actually mourned for us, VerseEnd Verse2 since she thought we died in the wilderness. She had also complained against my father, telling him he was a dreamer, saying: 2PSI You’ve led us out from our own land, and my sons are dead, and we’re going to die in the wilderness. VerseEnd Verse3 My mother complained like this against my father. VerseEnd Verse4 And my father told her: I know I’m a man of visions. However, if I hadn’t seen the things of God in a vision, I wouldn’t have known God’s goodness but would have stayed at Jerusalem and lost my life with my people. VerseEnd Verse5 But I’ve obtained a promised land, and I rejoice in that. I know the Lord will protect my sons from Laban and bring them back down to us in the wilderness. VerseEnd Verse6 This was how my father Lehi comforted my mother Sariah about us while we went through the wilderness up to Jerusalem to get the record of the Jews. VerseEnd Verse7 When we had returned to my father’s tent, their joy was complete and my mother was comforted. VerseEnd Verse8 She said: Now I know for sure the Lord has commanded my husband to escape into the wilderness. I also know for certain the Lord has protected my sons and rescued them from Laban and given them power so they were able to accomplish what He had commanded them to do. These were her new remarks. VerseEnd

Verse9 They were very glad and offered sacrifice and burnt offerings to the Lord and gave thanks to the God of Israel. VerseEnd Verse10 After thanking the God of Israel, my father Lehi took the records engraved on the brass plates and carefully studied them from the beginning. VerseEnd Verse11 He saw they contained the five books of Moses, which gave an account of the world’s creation and of Adam and Eve, who were our first parents; VerseEnd Verse12 and a record of the Jews from the beginning down to the start of the rule of Zedekiah, king of Judah; VerseEnd Verse13 and the prophecies of the holy prophets from the beginning, all the way up to the start of Zedekiah’s rule; and many prophecies of Jeremiah. VerseEnd Verse14 My father Lehi also found his ancestors’ genealogy on the brass plates; therefore he knew he was a descendant of Joseph, that same Joseph who was Jacob’s son, who was sold into Egypt and kept safe by the hand of the Lord so that he could keep his father and his whole household from dying of starvation. VerseEnd Verse15 They had also been saved from slavery and escaped from Egypt by that same God who kept them alive. VerseEnd Verse16 This was how my father discovered his ancestors’ genealogy. Laban was a descendant of Joseph too; therefore he and his forefathers had kept the records. VerseEnd Verse17 When my father saw all these things, he was filled with the Spirit and began to prophesy about his descendants: VerseEnd Verse18 that these brass plates would go to all nations, tribes, languages, and people who came from his descendants. VerseEnd Verse19 Therefore he said these brass plates would never be lost or obscured any more by time. And he prophesied many things about his descendants. VerseEnd

Verse20 Up to this point, my father and I had kept the commandments the Lord had given us. VerseEnd Verse21 We had obtained the records the Lord had commanded us to obtain and had studied them carefully, finding they were valuable and important for us so that we could retain the Lord’s commandments for our children. VerseEnd Verse22 That being the case, it was God’s wisdom for us to take them with us as we traveled in the wilderness to the promised land. VerseEnd
